Rashi on Keritot 4b:10:1.hebrew: לאו מלאו ולאו מכרת למידין - דבר מעניינו, בין לאו מלאו — כגון בעלמא גבי אבר מן חי בפ' (כל הבשר) (חולין קב.) — בין לאו מכרת, כגון הכא, מה כרת בקדשים, אף לאו בקדשים:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:10:1.english: We derive a prohibition from a prohibition and a prohibition from karet - [That is, we derive] a matter from its context, whether a prohibition from a prohibition — such as elsewhere regarding a limb from a living animal in the chapter [entitled] (Kol HaBasar) (Chullin 102a) — or a prohibition from karet, such as here: just as karet [is written] regarding consecrated [animals], so too the prohibition [is written] regarding consecrated [animals].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:10:2.hebrew: ורבנן סברי לאו מלאו הוא דילפינן - כי התם, אבל לאו מכרת לא ילפינן, הלכך בחולין כתיב. ואף בזו הספרים משובשים, וכולה גרסא ליתא:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:10:2.english: And the Rabbis maintain [that] it is a prohibition from a prohibition that we derive - As there [in the case of a limb from a living animal], but we do not derive a prohibition from karet; therefore, [the prohibition] is written with regard to non-sacrificial [animals]. And in this [passage] too, the texts are corrupted, and the entire reading is not [in the text].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:11:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: <abbr title="תנו רבנן">ת"ר</abbr>: "כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו" — <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> יהודה אומר: מה חלב לוקה שתים, אף דם לוקה שתים, <abbr title="וחכמים אומרים">וחכ"א</abbr>: אין בו אלא אזהרה אחת:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:11:1.english: This is the [correct] reading: The Sages taught: "You shall eat neither fat nor blood" — Rabbi Yehuda says: Just as [for] fat one is flogged two [sets of lashes], so too [for] blood one is flogged two [sets of lashes]; and the Sages say: There is only one prohibition regarding it.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:12:1.hebrew: מאי שנא חלב - כלומר, מ"ט כתביה לדם בהדי חלב? ליכתביה באנפי נפשיה, ואנא ידענא דלוקה ב', דמ"ש חלב דלוקה שתים בלא הקישא? כלומר, דם נמי כתיבי ב' קראי, אי הוה כתיב באנפי נפשיה — כגון "כל דם לא תאכלו" לכתוב ב"חקת עולם" — ל"ל דכתיב בהדי חלב:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:12:1.english: What is different [about] fat - That is to say, what is the reason [Scripture] wrote blood together with fat? Let it write it by itself, and I would know that one is flogged twice [for it], for what is different [about] fat that one is flogged twice without a juxtaposition? That is to say, [regarding] blood as well, two verses are written, if it had been written by itself — for instance, [if Scripture] had written "any blood you shall not eat" in [the verse] "an eternal statute" — why do I need it to be written together with fat?

Rashi on Keritot 4b:15:1.hebrew: דם אימעיט ממעילה בסוף כל הבשר בשחיטת חולין (דף קיז:), ואימא: כי היכי דאימעיט מזרות קרבן מעילה, אימעיט נמי ממלקות דזרות; קמ"ל:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:15:1.english: Blood is excluded from [the laws of] me'ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property] at the end of [the chapter] Kol HaBasar in Shechitat Chullin (117b); and I might say [that] just as it is excluded from a non-priest's me'ilah offering, it is also excluded from lashes for [consumption as] a non-priest — [therefore, the juxtaposition] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:15:2.hebrew: ה"ג: ס"ד אמינא: הואיל ואימעיט ממעילה, אימעיט נמי מזרות, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:15:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: It might enter your mind to say: Since [blood] was excluded from misuse of consecrated property [me'ilah], it was also excluded from [the prohibition of] a non-priest; [the juxtaposition] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:16:1.hebrew: אלא לרבנן - כיון דתרצינן דלר' יהודה לא בעי הקישא אלא משום זרות, ורבנן פליגי עליה ואמרי אין בו אלא אזהרה אחת, מכלל דסבירא להו מזרות נמי אימעיט, ולדידהו הקישא ל"ל:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:16:1.english: But according to the Rabbis - Since we resolved that according to Rabbi Yehuda, the juxtaposition is needed only because of [the prohibition of] non-priesthood, and the Rabbis disagree with him and say there is only one prohibition regarding it, it follows that they hold it is also excluded from [the prohibition of] non-priesthood; and according to them, why is the juxtaposition [needed]?

Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:1.hebrew: מה חלב מיוחד שחלבו חלוק מבשרו - שלא נאמר איסור חלב אלא בשור וכשב ועז, שחלבן אסור ובשרן מותר:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:1.english: Just as fat is unique in that its fat is distinct from its flesh - For the prohibition of [forbidden] fat was stated only regarding an ox, a sheep, and a goat, whose fat is forbidden while their flesh is permitted.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:2.hebrew: ואינן מצטרפין זה עם זה - לאיסור שבה, שהרי אין כאן אלא איסור החלב לבדו, ואין היתר מצטרף לאיסור, חוץ מאיסורי נזיר:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:2.english: And they do not combine with each other - For the prohibition that is in it, since there is here only the prohibition of the fat alone, and permitted [food] does not combine with forbidden [food], except for the prohibitions of a nazirite.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:3.hebrew: אף דם - אע"פ שאיסורו נוהג בטמאין, וראוי להצטרף הדם והבשר להתחייב בכזית משניהן משום טמא, לא יצטרפו, שנלמד דם מחלב: מה החלב על כרחיה לחלקו מפרידו מלהצטרף, שהרי חלוקין — זה לאיסור וזה להיתר, דאין איסור והיתר מצטרפים — אף דם הטמאים, הואיל ודמן חלוק מבשרן, שיש על הדם איסור כרת משום דם מה שאין כן בבשר, אינו מצטרף אפילו לענין (איסור) לטמא:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:17:3.english: So too, blood - Although its prohibition applies to non-kosher [animals], and [therefore] the blood and the flesh would be fit to combine to make one liable for an olive-bulk from both of them on account of [eating] a non-kosher [animal], they do not combine, because blood is derived from [forbidden] fat: just as [with] fat, its distinction perforce separates it from combining — since they are distinct, this one for prohibition and this one for permission, as a prohibited [substance] and a permitted [substance] do not combine — so too the blood of non-kosher [animals], since their blood is distinct from their flesh, in that there is a prohibition of karet upon the blood on account of [it being] blood, which is not the case with the flesh, it does not combine [with the flesh] even with respect to (the prohibition of) a non-kosher [animal].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:18:1.hebrew: יצאו שרצים - מדין ההיקש הזה, הואיל ואין דמן חלוק מבשרן — שאינו מוזהר על דמן משום דם אלא משום שרץ, כדאמרי' בפר' דם שחיטה (לקמן כריתות כא:): יצאו שרצים שאין בהן טומאה קלה כו'. הילכך מצטרפין זה עם זה, שהרי שם אחד להן. הילכך דם נחש ובשרו מצטרפין, דאין מוזהר על דמן משום דם, כדאמרינן בפרק דם שחיטה (שם), שאין אזהרת דם אלא בבהמה חיה ועוף כו':
Rashi on Keritot 4b:18:1.english: Creeping animals are excluded - From the law of this juxtaposition, since their blood is not distinct from their flesh — for one is not cautioned against [consuming] their blood on account of [the prohibition of] blood, but rather on account of [the prohibition of] a creeping animal, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Dam Shechitah (below, Keritot 21b): "Creeping animals are excluded, for they do not have lenient impurity, etc." Therefore, they combine with one another, for they have one designation. Therefore, the blood of a snake and its flesh combine, since one is not cautioned against their blood on account of [the prohibition of] blood, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Dam Shechitah (ibid.), that the prohibition of blood applies only to a domesticated animal, a wild beast, and a bird, etc.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:19:1.hebrew: דם שרץ מוזה נפקא - דאי ללמוד לשרץ גופיה, הא כתיב "אלה הטמאים לכם":
Rashi on Keritot 4b:19:1.english: The blood of a creeping animal is derived from "And this" - For if [it were written] to teach regarding the creeping animal itself, behold, it is [already] written: "These are they that are impure for you" [Leviticus 11:31].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:1:1.hebrew: לענין קרבן - וברייתא דלעיל בקרבן קמיירי, דגבי חטאות כתיב "ועשה מאחת מהנה":
Rashi on Keritot 4b:1:1.english: With regard to an offering - And the baraita [cited] above deals with an offering, for regarding sin offerings it is written: "and does [any] one of them" [Leviticus 4:2].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:20:1.english: With regard to ritual impurity - For [the measure of] a lentil-bulk.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:20:2.english: With regard to consumption - [combining to] an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:21:1.english: Therefore - since you said [that for] anything whose blood is not distinct from its flesh, [the blood and flesh] combine.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:21:2.hebrew: נחש נמי - אע"ג דלאו בר טומאה הוא, מצטרף דמו לבשרו לכזית לאכילה, דאין מוזהרין על דמו אלא משום בשרו:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:21:2.english: A snake also - Even though it is not subject to ritual impurity, its blood combines with its flesh to [constitute] an olive-bulk for eating, for one is not warned regarding its blood except on account of its flesh.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:21:3.hebrew: דאיתרבו לטומאה - כדאמרן, "וזה לכם הטמא" לימד על דם השרץ ובשרו שמצטרפין לטומאה:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:21:3.english: That are included with regard to ritual impurity - As we said [earlier], [the verse] "And this is for you the impure" taught regarding the blood of a creeping animal and its flesh that they combine with regard to ritual impurity.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:22:1.hebrew: ג' כריתות - תרין באחרי מות, וחד בצו את אהרן:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:22:1.english: Three [mentions of] karet - Two in [the Torah portion of] Acharei Mot, and one in [the Torah portion of] Tzav et Aharon.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:24:1.hebrew: ואפי' לר' יהודה - לא נפקא ליה דם התמצית מחד מהנך כריתות:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:24:1.english: And even according to Rabbi Yehuda - [the karet for] blood of exudate is not derived by him from one of these [mentions of] karet.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:25:2.hebrew: מה ת"ל כל דם - באחרי מות: "איש איש מבית ישראל ומן הגר הגר בתוכם אשר יאכל כל דם ונתתי פני וגו'". אין לי שיהא בכרת אלא דם קדשים שהנפש יוצאה בו, שמתכפר בו, שראוי לכפרה על המזבח, דהא כפרה כתיבא הכא: "ואני נתתיו לכם על המזבח לכפר", והני הוא דראויין לכפרה:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:25:2.english: What [is the meaning when] the verse states “any manner of blood” - In [the Torah portion] Acharei Mot [it is written]: “Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among them, that eats any manner of blood, I will set My face, etc.” I would only have [derived] that one is [liable to] excision for the blood of consecrated [offerings] with which the life departs, through which atonement is made, [and] which is fit for atonement upon the altar; for atonement is written here: “And I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement,” and these [types of blood] are the ones that are fit for atonement.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:26:1.hebrew: דם חולין ודם התמצית - לקדשים, דאינם ראוין לכפרה, כדאמרינן בסוף תמיד נשחט בפסחים (דף סה.):
Rashi on Keritot 4b:26:1.english: Blood of a non-sacred [animal] and blood of exudate - [i.e., blood of exudate] of consecrated [animals], as they are not fit for atonement, as we say at the end of [the chapter] Tamid Nishchat in Pesachim (65a).

Rashi on Keritot 4b:27:1.hebrew: אלא - לעולם רבנן, דלא נפקא לחולין מריבויא דקרא דכל, ואע"ג דלית להו כרת בדם התמצית, מיבעי להו חד כרת לדם כיסוי — לדם חיה ועוף שכיסהו ונתגלה. סד"א: בטלה אגב ארעא, ואי הדר אכלה עפרא בעלמא הוא ולא ליחייב, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:27:1.english: Rather - Actually, [Rava holds like] the Rabbis, that [karet] for non-sacred [blood] is not derived from the amplification of the verse "any [blood]." And even though they do not hold [that there is] karet for the blood of exudate, they need one [mention of] karet for the blood of covering — [i.e.,] for the blood of an undomesticated animal or a bird that one covered and it became uncovered. It might have entered your mind to say [that] it became nullified in the earth, and if one goes back and eats it, it is merely dirt and one should not be liable; [therefore, the verse] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:28:1.hebrew: ה' לאוין - הנך דלא אתו לדרשה: חד (ויקרא ג׳:י״ז) דחקת עולם, וחד בצו את אהרן (שם ז) כל דם לא תאכלו בכל מושבותיכם, וחד באחרי מות (שם יז) דם כל בשר לא תאכלו, וחד בראה אנכי (דברים י״ב:ט״ז) לא תאכלו על הארץ תשפכנו כמים — הרי ה'. ודכתיב לעיל מיניה לא תאכל הנפש עם הבשר, באבר מן החי משתעי. ודכתיב בתריה לא תאכלנו, מוקמינן בפרק כל הבשר בשחיטת חולין (דף קטו:) אזהרה לבשר בחלב. ועוד כתיב בראה אנכי רק את דמו לא תאכלו, ומוקמינן ליה בפרק שני דבכורות (דף טו.) לחלב פסולי המוקדשים. ודכתיב באחרי מות כל נפש מכם לא תאכל דם, מוקים ליה תורת כהנים להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:28:1.english: Five prohibitions - Those that do not come for a [specific] exposition: one (Leviticus 3:17) [is the verse] of "a perpetual statute"; and one in [the portion of] Tzav et Aharon (ibid. 7), "You shall eat no blood in any of your dwellings"; and one in [the portion of] Acharei Mot (ibid. 17), "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh"; and one in [the portion of] Re'eh Anochi (Deuteronomy 12:16), "You shall not eat it; you shall pour it upon the earth as water" — behold, [that is] five. And that which is written above it, "You shall not eat the life with the flesh," speaks of a limb from a living animal. And that which is written after it, "You shall not eat it," we establish in the chapter Kol HaBasar in Shechitat Chullin (115b) [as] a prohibition for meat with milk. And furthermore it is written in Re'eh Anochi, "Only you shall not eat its blood," and we establish it in the second chapter of Bekhorot (15a) for the fat of disqualified consecrated animals. And that which is written in Acharei Mot, "No person among you shall eat blood," Torat Kohanim establishes it to warn adults regarding minors.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:29:1.hebrew: א"ר אילא אכל מעשר - שני של דגן ותירוש ויצהר, לוקה ג', משום לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך וגו':
Rashi on Keritot 4b:29:1.english: Rabbi Illa said: [If] one ate [the] tithe - [Meaning, the] second [tithe] of grain, wine, and oil, he is flogged [with] three [sets of lashes], on account of [the verse], "You may not eat within your gates," etc.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:2:1.hebrew: הב"ע - הא דקתני ב' שמות, כגון שאכלן בב' תמחוין, ב' מאכלין דהיינו ב' שמות, כגון תבשיל וצלי:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:2:1.english: What are we dealing with here - That which [it] teaches [regarding] two categories [is] a case where he ate them from two dishes, [i.e.,] two [types of] foods, which are two categories, such as a cooked dish and a roast.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:2:2.hebrew: (ל"א: חייב ב' - א' משום חלב, וא' משום קדש — אשם מעילה — ודלא כר' יהודה, דמחייב משום חלב שתים, משום ב' לאוין דכתיבי בחלב בתרי פסוקי):
Rashi on Keritot 4b:2:2.english: (Alternate version: He is liable for two [offerings] - one on account of [forbidden] fat and one on account of sacred [property] — a guilt offering for misappropriation — and [this is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who holds [him] liable for two [offerings] on account of [forbidden] fat, because of the two negative commandments that are written regarding [forbidden] fat in two verses.)

Rashi on Keritot 4b:2:3.english: Of Rabbi Yehoshua - In the chapter [entitled] Ameru Lo (below, Keritot 15b).

Rashi on Keritot 4b:31:1.english: With a positive commandment - A prohibition derived from a positive commandment [has the status of] a positive commandment.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:4:1.hebrew: תרי קראי - חד בקדשים, "חוקת עולם", וחד בין בחולין בין בקדשים. הילכך, בחלב המוקדשים איכא שני לאוין משום חלב. וחלב חולין נפקא ליה לר' יהודה כדאמרינן בפ' אלו עוברין (פסחים מג:): "כי כל אוכל חלב מן הבהמה" — אין לי אלא חלב תמימין הראוי ליקרב, חלב בעלי מומין מנין? תלמוד לומר "כל חלב", חולין מנין? תלמוד לומר "כי כל":
Rashi on Keritot 4b:4:1.english: Two verses - One [deals] with consecrated [animals]: "a perpetual statute," and one [applies] both to non-sacred [animals] and to consecrated [animals]. Therefore, with regard to the forbidden fat of consecrated [animals], there are two prohibitions on account of forbidden fat. And [the prohibition of] forbidden fat of non-sacred [animals] is derived by Rabbi Yehuda as we say in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 43b): "For whoever eats fat from the animal" — I have [derived] only the fat of unblemished [animals] that is fit to be offered; from where [do I derive] the fat of blemished [animals]? The verse states: "all fat"; from where [do I derive] non-sacred [animals]? The verse states: "For all."

Rashi on Keritot 4b:5:1.hebrew: קסברי רבנן לאו דחקת עולם בקדשים - דהא בעניינא דקדשים כתיב, ולאו דכל חלב בחולין ולא בקדשים:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:5:1.english: The Rabbis maintain [that] the prohibition of “a perpetual statute” [was stated] with regard to sacrificial [animals] - For it is written in the passage of sacrificial [animals], and the prohibition of “any fat” [was stated] with regard to non-sacred [animals] and not with regard to sacrificial [animals].

Rashi on Keritot 4b:6:1.hebrew: ה"ג אבל דחולין דאסור חלבו אימא לא - והכי פירושא: אבל חולין דקילי, אימא לא אסיר חלבו. דאסור חלבו אימא לא — כלומר, אימא לא אסור חלבו. ולשון הפוך היא, לשון גרסא ירושלמית:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:6:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "But [as for] non-sacred [animals], that its fat is forbidden, say not" - And this is its explanation: But [as for] non-sacred [animals], which are lenient, say [that] its fat is not forbidden. "That its fat is forbidden, say not" — that is to say, say [that] its fat is not forbidden. And it is an inverted expression, [in] the style of a Jerusalemite reading.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:7:1.hebrew: חלב מוקדשין הותר מכללו - דהא אליה איקרי חלב בכבש, ואישתראי בשור ועז:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:7:1.english: The fat of consecrated [animals] was permitted from its general [prohibition] - For the fat-tail is called "fat" [chelev] in [the case of] a sheep, yet it is permitted in [the case of] an ox and a goat.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:8:1.hebrew: ור' יהודה סבר כי כתיב נמי כו' - כדאמרן לעיל:
Rashi on Keritot 4b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda maintains [that] when it is also written, etc. - As we said above.

Rashi on Keritot 4b:9:1.english: By inference that the Rabbis do not derive - [This is asked] in astonishment.
